subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Potter Sequence, Pulmonary Hypoplasia and Amnioinfusion

steps.tx: The constellation of flattened facies, limb deformities and lung hypoplasia from prolonged absent fluid is the **Potter sequence**. It follows bilateral renal agenesis or prolonged early rupture. Pulmonary hypoplasia, not the kidney failure, is what kills at birth. The sequence is mechanical, so any cause of prolonged zero fluid, renal or rupture, gives the same face and limbs.
steps.say: Potter sequence flattens features and hypoplases lungs from prolonged absent fluid.

steps.tx: Failure of lung growth from chronic compression and absent fluid cycling is **pulmonary hypoplasia**. Earlier and longer fluid loss gives worse hypoplasia. It determines survival in prolonged preterm rupture cases. Rupture before 24 weeks with fluid still absent weeks later is the history that most worries neonatologists.
steps.say: Pulmonary hypoplasia from chronic fluid loss determines survival after prolonged rupture.

steps.tx: Removing excess fluid therapeutically by needle is **amnioreduction**. It eases maternal symptoms and may prolong pregnancy in twin transfusion recipients before laser. Volumes of one to two litres are removed slowly. One to two litres drained over about twenty minutes, then slowed, keeps placental separation risk down.
steps.say: Amnioreduction removes one to two litres slowly to ease symptoms.

steps.tx: Instilling saline into the uterus to restore fluid for scanning or labour is **amnioinfusion**. It clarifies anatomy in oligohydramnios and cushions the cord against variable decelerations. Infection risk limits its diagnostic use to selected cases. Intrapartum infusion uses warmed saline through an intrauterine catheter and eases recurrent variable decelerations.
steps.say: Amnioinfusion restores fluid to clarify anatomy and cushion the cord in labour.

steps.tx: The prostaglandin inhibitor reducing fetal urine output to treat polyhydramnios is **indomethacin**. It risks premature ductus closure, so use is short and monitored. Maternal gastric and fetal cardiac surveillance accompany it. Treatment courses are kept under a week where possible, with ductus Doppler checks during use.
steps.say: Indomethacin reduces fetal urine for polyhydramnios but risks ductus closure.

steps.tx: Fibrous bands amputating fetal parts after membrane rupture form the **amniotic band** sequence. Asymmetric limb and body wall defects result. It is a disruption, not an inherited malformation, so recurrence is negligible. Constriction rings with lymphoedema beyond the band separate it from inherited limb reduction defects.
steps.say: Amniotic bands amputate fetal parts asymmetrically with negligible recurrence risk.

steps.tx: Serial amnioinfusion for early renal oligohydramnios is experimental and offered only in trials, termed **investigational therapy**. Families need frank discussion of pulmonary prognosis regardless of kidney options. Neonatal dialysis planning forms part of counselling. Consent must state plainly that lung development, not kidney replacement, limits survival in most cases.
steps.say: Serial amnioinfusion for renal oligohydramnios remains investigational within trials only.

steps.tx: Clubbed limbs and flattened nose with low set ears are the visible **Potter facies**. They result from mechanical compression without fluid cushioning. Their presence at birth confirms prolonged severe oligohydramnios. Low set floppy ears and a flattened nose with recessed chin make the classic Potter facies description.
steps.say: Potter facies shows flattened nose and low ears from prolonged fluid absence.

steps.tx: Fluid assessment anchors decisions in growth restriction and rupture alike, summarised as **fluid centred surveillance**. Trends in deepest pool accompany Doppler at every review. Sudden fluid falls prompt delivery discussions at viable gestations. A single deepest pool that keeps falling week by week earns delivery planning even when growth holds.
steps.say: Fluid centred surveillance trends deepest pool with Doppler at every review.
